source.title: Quantum versus thermal fluctuations in phase transitions of two-dimensional superconductors

model.hamiltonian: H = -t * sum_<ij> cos(phi_i - phi_j) + (U/2) * sum_i (-i d/dphi_i)^2

path_integral_mapping.action: S = -sum_(tau,<ij>) K_s cos(phi_i(tau)-phi_j(tau)) - sum_(tau,i) K_tau cos(phi_i(tau)-phi_i(tau+Delta_tau))
path_integral_mapping.mapping: 2D quantum rotor -> anisotropic 3D classical phase action

source_notes: The authors state Metropolis moves help avoid slowing down near criticality where Wolff clusters become comparable to the system size.
Spatial and imaginary-time couplings are anisotropic at finite Delta_tau.
N_tau must be increased and Delta_tau extrapolated; small imaginary-time discretisation can systematically underestimate stiffness.

quantum_critical_point.method: linear extrapolation of finite-Delta_tau critical interactions to Delta_tau -> 0

universality.critical_size_relation: Upsilon * L is size-independent at U_c when z=1

regimes: For U < U_c, finite-temperature BKT behavior remains and the transition temperature decreases with U.
For U > U_c, the paper reports finite resistance at all studied nonzero temperatures and a metallic-to-insulating crossover.

The total vortex density grows with U and remains finite at low temperature in the studied quantum regime; the reported total vortex count does not separate bound vortex-antivortex pairs from free vortices.

transport.continuation_method: Constrained Lorentzian plus symmetrized Gaussian in the normal phase; symmetrized Gaussian in the superconducting phase
limitations: Analytic continuation is ill-conditioned because current-current data contain Monte Carlo statistical noise.
The source explicitly reports that finite-size effects prevent physically reliable continuation near the critical temperature.
The assumed continuation basis is a source-specific ansatz and is not a uniquely determined spectrum.

claim_ceiling: Literature source record only. These are paper-reported model and numerical results; Symthaea has not independently reproduced the QMC calculations or measured a material.
